name: Vistra
description: Vistra is not a regulated utility: it owns 43,641 MW of power plants and sells the electricity at market prices, wholesale and through its own retail brands (TXU Energy is the best known). About 62 percent of capacity is natural gas, 20 percent coal, 15 percent nuclear (six reactors, 6,448 MW) and 3 percent solar and batteries. The retail arm is a natural hedge: it buys the plants' output and sells to homes and businesses in 16 states. The story has shifted to selling carbon-free nuclear power to data center users: a 2,609 MW agreement with Meta from PJM nuclear plants and a 20-year, 1,200 MW agreement with Amazon Web Services at Comanche Peak. Results are volatile because wholesale prices, weather and hedge marks move revenue (unrealized hedging was a $766M loss in 2025).
